clue.text: Irish classic pub gets in a few kegs an' rum

indicators.note: the pub gets in among the other letters, sitting inside them
rum means odd or strange, so the preceding letters are put into a strange order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An Irish pub famed for its beer and spirits squeezes in a few kegs and some rum.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'a few kegs an'' wrap round the pub after their first letter, giving FINNEGANS WAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce's Finnegans Wake is a famously difficult novel and a classic of Irish literature.

clue.text: Most of wardrobe thrown out, getting more pants

indicators.note: things thrown out are tossed about, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: all three words are taken letter for letter, not as an instruction to shorten

explanation.surface: Clearing out most of a wardrobe and ending up buying even more underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' looks like a deletion instruction, but those words are themselves fodder. Pants is British slang for rubbish, as well as underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Going from bad to worse means steadily deteriorating, which in British slang is becoming ever more pants (rubbish).

clue.text: Article stolen from ME country upset philanthropist

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top
something stolen from a place is taken away, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: a country of the Middle East

explanation.surface: A news story about a philanthropist upset at an item stolen from a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is the Middle East. Take AN out of LEBANON to leave LEBON, then read it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel left his fortune to fund the Nobel Prizes, making him a famous philanthropist.

clue.text: Senior job at paper? Oh Piers … it'd run into trouble!

indicators.note: letters that run into trouble are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter, the dots and apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone warns Piers (Morgan, perhaps) that taking the top job at a newspaper would end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Piers Morgan once edited British tabloids, which gives the surface its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The editorship is the most senior post at a newspaper, held by the person in charge of its content.

clue.text: American drug cop hastily cleared out — total chaos!

parts.note: US slang for a narcotics agent

indicators.note: a word cleared out has its contents emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: An American narcotics officer leaves in a hurry amid complete chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is total lawlessness and disorder, an absence of any controlling authority.

clue.text: A bit of sushi at suppertime — it's traditional in Japan

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: a thing that is traditional in Japan

indicators.note: a bit of the following words is a run of consecutive letters lifted from them

parts.note: the letters run across the words sushi, at and suppertime

explanation.surface: Eating a little sushi with the evening meal is a Japanese custom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to food, but the answer is a Japanese massage therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a traditional Japanese form of finger-pressure massage, so it is a practice traditional in Japan.

clue.text: Crooked penny once spent by much-loved railway author

indicators.note: a penny spent is gone, so that letter is used up and removed

parts.note: the Rev W. Awdry wrote the Thomas the Tank Engine books
the pre-decimal British penny was abbreviated d

explanation.surface: A beloved writer about railways once spent a bent penny.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the old-money penny, D, from AWDRY to leave AWRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awry is askew or out of its proper line, which is to say crooked.

clue.text: Screened copper summoned to murder trial

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... Morse, the young detective of the TV series ..., called to a murder scene
second meaning: an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: A TV detective is called in to give evidence at a murder trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' looks like part of the courtroom picture, but it stands alone as the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Endeavour was the ITV prequel to Inspector Morse, named for his first name; an endeavour is also an attempt, a trial.

clue.text: Looking glum and about to spit feathers?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: with fluffy plumage in one's mouth, ready to be spat out

explanation.surface: Someone looks miserable and is about to explode with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit feathers' is a British idiom for being furious, which seems to match the glum mood; read literally, feathers would be down in your mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Down in the mouth is an idiom for dispirited; down is soft feathering, so it is also the literal state before spitting.

clue.text: Order balti and gobi as essential accompaniments

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the two dish names, with 'and' only joining them

explanation.surface: At the curry house, ordering a balti with gobi (cauliflower) as must-have side dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as asking a waiter, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Obbligati are musical parts that must not be omitted, so they are indispensable accompaniments.

clue.text: Lover boy's half-hearted equestrian event

indicators.note: the heart of the word is halved in value, so its middle letter is swapped for a smaller one

explanation.surface: A romantic young man shows only lukewarm enthusiasm for a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of ROMEO is M, Roman numeral 1000; half of that is 500, which is D. Swap M for D to get RODEO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a competition of riding skills on horses and bulls, so it is an equestrian event.

clue.text: Bowled over, carrying one pound sword

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it inside, so these letters go within the others

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked flat while lugging a hefty one-pound sword.
explanation.walkthrough: B and O sit outside, with I and LB carried between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilbo is an old type of sword, named after Bilbao in Spain, which was famed for its blades.

clue.text: Pretty smart

definitions.meaning: first meaning: attractive in an endearing way

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'fairly clever', with pretty as an adverb, but each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both endearing attractiveness and, especially in American use, sharp cleverness.

clue.text: First signs of dew attracting warblers near daybreak

indicators.note: the first sign of each word is its opening letter

parts.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Early-morning dew draws songbirds as the day breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' looks like part of the scene but its first letter is needed; the definition is the final word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the first light of morning, the moment of daybreak.

clue.text: Large part of Merseyside embracing northern singer

indicators.note: to embrace something is to put your arms round it, so it ends up inside

parts.note: Crosby is a town north of Liverpool in Merseyside

explanation.surface: A big area of Merseyside welcomes a singer from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large part' reads as one phrase, but Large alone gives BIG, which wraps N.
explanation.definitionFit: Bing Crosby was the American crooner famous for White Christmas.

clue.text: Barman Claude Eddery regularly stealing kiss

indicators.note: something stolen is taken in and held, so the other word goes inside
taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss

explanation.surface: A bartender named Claude Eddery sneaks a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is not a bartender: a composer writes music in bars. Pat Eddery was a famous British jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy, the French composer, is a man of musical bars, so a witty 'barman' named Claude.

clue.text: Manage a rising cosmetic firm that originated in Brazil

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: something that originated in Brazil

parts.note: to boss is to direct or run

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Running an up-and-coming beauty company with Brazilian roots.
explanation.walkthrough: AVON read upwards gives NOVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bossa nova is a style of music and dance that emerged in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in the late 1950s.

clue.text: One with a fabulous body seen in tunic or negligee

indicators.note: the answer can be seen sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across tunic, or and negligee

explanation.surface: Someone with a fantastic figure looks good in either a tunic or a negligee.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous here means belonging to fable, not gorgeous.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicorn is a mythical creature, so its body belongs in fables: a fabulous body in the literal sense.

clue.text: Turfing out old uniform Police leader

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Sting was the frontman of the band The Police

explanation.surface: A senior police officer ejects someone in an outdated uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police leader' is not a chief constable but the lead singer of the rock band The Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting means forcing someone out of a place or position, which is turfing them out.

clue.text: Energy-saving kitchen implement is more sublime

indicators.note: a saving holds on to something, keeping it stored inside

parts.note: a tool for shredding cheese and the like

explanation.surface: An energy-efficient kitchen gadget is something special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy-saving' reads as eco-friendly, but it means the implement keeps E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater can mean grander or nobler, so it is a comparative of lofty or sublime.

clue.text: Painter of sacred, half-neglected cloistered yard

indicators.note: with half of a word neglected, only the other half is kept

parts.note: a garth is the enclosed garden of a cloister

explanation.surface: An artist of holy subjects paints a monastery courtyard gone half to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the first half of HOLY and add GARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and engraver, famous for A Rake's Progress.

clue.text: Greeting to welcome King of France in Barnet, Sheen

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so this goes inside

explanation.surface: A greeting for a French king visiting the London districts of Barnet and Sheen.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet and Sheen look like London places, but barnet is rhyming slang (Barnet Fair) for hair, so a Barnet sheen is a gloss for the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair oil is a product that gives the hair a glossy sheen, so it is literally shine for your barnet.

clue.text: Best if Tim shed a stone

indicators.note: something shed is cast off, so those letters are dropped

explanation.surface: It would be ideal if Tim lost a stone (14 pounds) in weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is 14 pounds in British weight, which the surface plays on; take TIM out of OPTIMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone, so it is a stone in the jewellery sense.

clue.text: Cap of stupid boy when cycling

indicators.note: letters cycling go round in a loop, moving from the front to the back

parts.note: 'Stupid boy' is Captain Mainwaring's catchphrase for Private Pike in the British sitcom Dad's Army

explanation.surface: A daft lad's headgear while out on his bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Move PI from the front to the back of PIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap with a flat circular top and a peak.

clue.text: Prepare to fight again and back leader of military

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Getting ready for renewed war while supporting the head of the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as a verb meaning support, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to supply with weapons once more, readying for further combat.

clue.text: Freeman from the south freed Muslim prince

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means going from the bottom upwards
a word freed is released from its bounds, so its outer letters fall away

explanation.surface: A southern freeman liberates an Islamic prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer letters of FREEMAN, then read the remainder upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer, or emir, is a title for a Muslim ruler or prince.

clue.text: Health resort put on starter of minced meat out of a tin

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A health spa serves tinned minced meat as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'put on' places the spa above the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the brand of processed pork luncheon meat sold in tins.

clue.text: Exclusive small store on the High Street

parts.note: the Co-op is a British chain of shops found on high streets

explanation.surface: A shop that is the only small store of its kind on the main street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exclusive' reads as an adjective but is the noun: a story only one newspaper has.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is a news story published by one paper ahead of rivals, an exclusive.

clue.text: Right, so picked up items for the wedding

indicators.note: words picked up are caught by ear, so we want how they sound

parts.note: true means right, and so stays as it is

explanation.surface: Just so: someone collects the things needed for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The French-derived word is pronounced roughly 'troo-so'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes, linen and other belongings a bride gathers for her marriage.

clue.text: "Art" — my radical new hotel opening in the West End

indicators.note: a new version is made over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An avant-garde art show at a new hotel launching in London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests a launch, but it means a gateway. The West End is central London's theatre and shopping area.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiralty Arch is a ceremonial archway in central London, between Trafalgar Square and The Mall, so it is literally an opening.
